paragraphs.text: Cloud City, Bespin. Three months after the Battle of Endor.

Han Solo had once been delivered to Cloud City in chains. This time, he arrived carrying the key. It was a small, unremarkable piece of Imperial technology, scarcely larger than a credit chip. Chewbacca had removed it from the communications buoy they had captured near Tatooine, and Han had spent most of the journey examining it. He understood very little about how it worked.

He did, however, understand what it was worth. Somebody had gone to considerable trouble to prevent him from obtaining it. Two armed interceptors, a falsified security authorization, and a small explosive charge were not the usual precautions taken to protect an ordinary communications component. Which meant it probably opened something interesting. And interesting things, Han had discovered, were frequently dangerous. The Millennium Falcon descended toward Cloud City's upper landing platforms.

Beyond the cockpit windows, the city gleamed in the sunlight. Its elegant towers rose above a vast ocean of golden clouds, looking every bit as peaceful as they had on his previous visit. Han frowned.
"Yeah, well, last time I said that, we ended up having a pretty lousy vacation."
The Wookiee gave a more elaborate response.
"No, I haven't forgotten the part where he handed us over to Vader."
Chewbacca looked at him. Han sighed.
"All right. We forgave him. Doesn't mean I can't complain."
He guided the Falcon toward the landing platform. Leia was waiting beside Lando Calrissian. Han smiled.
Leia embraced him before he could make another joke. For a moment, Han simply held her. Then she stepped back and examined his face.
Chewbacca emerged from the Falcon and released an enormous, incredulous roar. Han closed his eyes.
Leia laughed. Lando approached with his arms spread.
"You're not going to offer me refreshments, are you?"
"And I'll apologize again if you like."
Chewbacca gave a satisfied rumble. Lando looked toward the enormous Wookiee.
"Wonderful. Now both of you are enjoying yourselves."
"Can we go? There's something important we need to examine."
Han held up the Imperial command key.

Commander Venn had prepared a secure examination room in Cloud City's administrative complex. The recovered Imperial archive from the hidden laboratory had been transferred there after Leia and Lando's previous investigation. Most of the records were accessible. But one section remained locked behind a security system requiring authorization from the Emperor's private household. The same type of authorization used by the intercepted communications buoy.
Han placed the key on the table. Venn examined it.
Venn regarded him for several seconds.
"General Solo, this is an Imperial executive authorization module."
"It could provide access to restricted military facilities across several sectors."
"Possibly. But I'd like to know what information it contains before we connect it to anything."
Chewbacca produced a low, approving growl. Han glanced at him.
Venn examined the module beneath a scanner. A series of symbols appeared. Then a name. SIM ALOO. Leia moved closer.
"One of Palpatine's advisers. He was aboard the second Death Star."
"Well, someone has been using his credentials."
"We know," Han said. "That's how somebody sent fake orders to a medical transport."
"These aren't merely copied credentials. The authorization contains a valid private signature."
"It means whoever issued this had access to one of the original authentication devices."

Venn enlarged the display. The command key had been used repeatedly since the Battle of Endor. Most of its activity concerned administrative systems. But several entries were more troubling. Military transport authorizations. Classified prisoner transfers. Access to former Imperial research facilities. Leia studied the list.
"Whoever's using this has been moving through the Empire's remaining infrastructure."
Venn gave him a stern look.
"Yeah. That's usually when I make jokes."

The archive opened seventeen minutes later. Venn had connected the command key to an isolated terminal, copying its authorization sequence while preventing it from establishing a connection to the wider Imperial network. The result was a directory of sealed research files. Most were associated with carbon preservation. But several belonged to a different project. HOLLOW THRONE — BESПIN RESEARCH DIVISION. Leia leaned forward.
The terminal requested a second authorization. Venn frowned.
"The system wants confirmation from an experimental subject."
"Someone whose physiological profile was recorded during a previous trial."
Lando's expression changed. He looked at Han. Then at Leia.
"Remember the records we found in the laboratory?"
"The ones from when you were frozen."
Han stared. For a moment, the humor vanished from his face.
"Imperial scientists were monitoring the freezing process."
"We don't think Vader knew about it."
Han considered this. Then looked back at the terminal.
"And somebody wants my permission to open the files?"
"Well, this is new. Usually people ask before they experiment on me."
The terminal displayed a biometric authorization request. Venn examined the available data.
"Apparently the researchers required the presence of an original observation subject to unlock the protected results."
"All right. Let's get it over with."
"We don't know what this machine does."
Han studied the equipment. Then he slowly withdrew his hand.
Venn examined the scanner again. A faint smile crossed her face.
"Fortunately, the original identification records contain enough biometric information to reconstruct the authorization."
She entered a sequence of commands. The terminal flashed. SUBJECT IDENTIFIED: HAN SOLO. A second line appeared. PRIMARY OBSERVATION SUBJECT: LEIA ORGANA. Han frowned.
Leia stared at the display. The next message appeared. EXPERIMENTAL RECORD ACCESS GRANTED. The directory opened. Han looked at Leia.
"Why do I get the feeling I'm not going to like this?"

The first recording showed the carbon-freezing chamber. Han recognized it immediately. The platform. The machinery. The enormous conduits running along the ceiling. He remembered the cold. The sound of Chewbacca roaring. Leia standing just beyond the platform. Then the terrible moment when the machinery began lowering him into the freezing pit. He had not seen the recording before. He had not particularly wanted to. Lando stood beside him.
Han looked at the image. His younger self stood on the platform, trying to appear considerably less frightened than he actually was.

The recording continued. Vader watched from the shadows. Imperial technicians worked at their controls. The platform descended. Then the image changed. A series of measurements appeared. Heart rate. Respiration. Neural activity. Memory-state indicators. Han stared.
"They were monitoring your neurological activity during carbon preservation."
"Apparently to determine whether complex memories and learned behaviors survived the process."
"That's a fancy way of saying experiment."

She did not argue. The recording advanced. The carbon-freezing process completed. A display confirmed that Han's brain activity had entered a state of suspended preservation. Then another series of readings appeared. These were not his. Leia recognized them immediately. They had been collected from the observation platform above the freezing chamber. From her. She watched as the data changed. Her heart rate accelerated. Her breathing became irregular.

The monitoring equipment recorded an intense emotional response. And then something unexpected happened. The scientists' own commentary appeared beside the readings. Primary observation subject displays attachment response significantly exceeding expected parameters. A second note followed. Response persists despite termination of direct sensory contact. Leia frowned.
"The researchers expected your physiological response to decline once Han was removed from view."

Han smiled faintly. But he was no longer entirely joking. He remembered what Leia had said before he was frozen. He remembered believing he might never see her again. And he remembered the warmth of her face amid the terrible cold. He turned back toward the recording.

The next file was a research memorandum. It had been written several days after Han's freezing, then amended following his recovery from carbonite on Tatooine. The report confirmed that his memories and personality had survived the process. That much was obvious. Han could remember being frozen. He could remember waking. He could certainly remember the discomfort of being temporarily blind. But the researchers had been interested in something more complicated.

"The experiment demonstrates that complex autobiographical memory can persist through prolonged physical suspension. However, attempts to isolate individual emotional associations have produced inconsistent results."
"Memories connected to particular people," Venn explained. "Relationships. Attachments. Things that matter to us personally."
"The scientists believed certain memories could be altered or suppressed without affecting the subject's professional abilities. But they encountered a persistent difficulty."
Venn opened an attached file. A hologram appeared. A woman sat in a chair inside a laboratory. She appeared calm. An unseen interviewer spoke.
"And how do you feel about that?"
Her voice was flat. The interviewer paused.
The recording continued. The interviewer placed a small object on the table. A child's toy. A battered little landspeeder. The woman's expression changed. Her fingers began trembling.
The interviewer said nothing. She reached for the toy. Then stopped. Tears filled her eyes.
The woman struggled to speak. Her breathing became irregular. Then she whispered a name. The recording stopped. Leia stared at the empty hologram.
"But the toy brought the memory back."
"Not entirely. According to the report, the woman continued obeying most imposed commands."
"The researchers discovered that certain memories remained accessible through associations they had not identified or suppressed."
Leia looked at the little toy frozen in the last frame.
"And the stronger the connection, the harder it was to remove."

Han leaned against the wall. He had heard enough. Not because the experiment was difficult to understand. Because he understood it too well. For years, he had thought of himself as a man who needed nobody. No obligations. No attachments. Just a ship, a good copilot, and enough money to stay ahead of his creditors. Then he had met Luke. And Leia.

And somewhere along the way, he had discovered that the people he once considered inconvenient had become the most important things in his life. The Empire had tried to take those things from him. Vader had frozen him. Jabba had displayed him like a trophy. And now he was discovering that Imperial scientists had studied the experience as though it were an interesting laboratory procedure. He felt anger rising.
He looked at her. For a moment, he considered making a joke. Then decided against it.
"And they were using what happened to us to hurt other people."

He looked back toward the terminal. The woman from the recording had remembered her brother. Despite everything. Despite the conditioning. Despite the Empire's efforts to erase him. Han exhaled slowly.
The next file was considerably older. It had been stored within a restricted directory labeled: WITNESS ZERO — ORIGINAL FAILURE. Venn frowned.
"The file predates the Bespin laboratory by more than twenty years."

The directory contained several scientific reports, though most were incomplete. The earliest records described an experiment conducted under the supervision of an unnamed private researcher. A man had been brought into a laboratory and exposed to a reconstructed voice. The researchers expected the subject to respond emotionally. Instead, he reported hearing something impossible. A voice belonging to someone who had died decades earlier. The next test produced a different result.
Another subject heard the same words, but in a different voice. Venn examined the transcript.
"Every subject reports hearing the same sentence."
Venn opened the recording. A woman's voice filled the room. Soft. Familiar. Leia froze. She knew that voice. She had not heard it in years.

Leia felt the blood drain from her face. It was her father's voice. Bail Organa. Not an approximation. Not a recording she recognized. His voice as she remembered it from childhood. Warm. Gentle. A little tired. She had heard it countless times in the gardens of the royal palace on Alderaan. She stared at the terminal.
Silence. Lando stared at both of them.

Nobody spoke. Venn examined the audio file. The waveform displayed only a brief burst of static. She replayed it through an isolated analysis system. Static again. Then the recording ended. Venn looked troubled.

They stared at the terminal. The transcript remained visible. I REMEMBER THE GARDEN. Leia read the words again. Her father had loved gardens. He had maintained a small private one in the palace, where he sometimes retreated after difficult Senate sessions. She remembered sitting beside him as a child, watching him tend delicate flowering plants brought from distant worlds. Had the machine somehow found that memory?
Or had something else happened? Venn examined the technical notes.
"The original researchers encountered the same phenomenon. Different subjects perceived different voices, even though the recording contained no identifiable speech."

Venn opened the final page. A short entry appeared. WITNESS ZERO — PROCEDURE TERMINATED. SUBJECT RESPONSE: INCONSISTENT. SOURCE IDENTITY: UNRESOLVED. RECOMMENDATION: DO NOT REPEAT WITHOUT DIRECT SUPERVISION. Leia stared at the final line.
Venn searched the metadata. Most of the information had been erased. But one field remained. ORIGINAL SPONSOR: DAMASK HOLDINGS. Lando frowned.
Leia looked toward Threepio, who had been quietly examining the records.
"Damask Holdings was a prominent financial organization during the final years of the Republic, Princess. It was controlled by a Muun financier named Hego Damask."
"A wealthy businessman with extensive political connections. He died shortly before Palpatine became Supreme Chancellor."

Leia stared at the name. The timing troubled her. An experiment involving voices and memories. Conducted before the Empire existed. Financed by a man who died just as Palpatine rose to power. She made a note.

The final archive contained the records Leia had been searching for. AUREL SEVEN — SUBJECT RETENTION PROGRAM. Forty-three prisoners. Alderaanian origin. Long-term experimental custody. The files included medical evaluations, psychological assessments, and transport records. Most names were concealed. But the accompanying notes revealed something the Emperor's researchers had struggled to understand. The prisoners had been unusually resistant to conditioning. Not because they possessed extraordinary abilities.

Not because they were immune to the machinery. But because they had repeatedly reinforced one another's memories. The researchers had attempted to isolate them. Even so, the captives developed elaborate methods of preserving their identities. Shared stories. Private jokes. Old songs. Memories of people they had loved. A report described one prisoner who had begun forgetting her own name. Another captive had spent three consecutive nights repeating it to her.

Along with the names of her parents. The street where she grew up. The flowers that bloomed beside her childhood home. By the fourth day, the prisoner remembered. The researchers classified the incident as a failure of memory suppression. Leia read it differently. The woman had been saved by someone who refused to let her disappear. She thought of Alderaan. Of the people she had lost. Of her father.

Of the thousands of stories that existed nowhere now except in the memories of those who had survived. And she understood something important. The Empire had destroyed her world. But it had not destroyed everything that world had been.
Han's voice brought her back. She looked up. He was watching her.

Venn opened the final transport record. The most recent entry had been created two days earlier. It showed a transfer of forty-three living subjects from one Imperial custodial facility to another. Leia studied the figures.
Leia closed her eyes briefly. Forty-three. Not merely names on an old list. Not a bookkeeping error. Forty-three people who might still be waiting for someone to find them.
Han held up the command key.
Venn tried. The terminal accepted the authorization. A series of routing references appeared. Then stopped. The destination remained concealed. Venn frowned.
"A segmented routing system. Each transfer station knows only the next destination. The complete route is held elsewhere."
"But the transfer used a civilian supply corridor. We may be able to identify the vessel by comparing its departure time with registered traffic."

Venn displayed it. A six-hour period. Several dozen vessels. Han began examining their registrations. Most were ordinary freighters. Medical transports. Supply ships. A handful of Imperial vessels operating under surrender agreements. Then he stopped.

Han pointed toward one entry. A medium transport registered to an Imperial logistics organization. Its departure time matched the encrypted transfer. Its cargo capacity was sufficient for forty-three passengers. And its declared cargo was medical equipment.

Han opened the vessel's history. The ship had made four journeys in the previous month. Each used a similar route. Each originated near a former Imperial detention facility. Each carried classified cargo. Han smiled.
"Not yet. But we know what ship we're looking for."
He copied the registration. IMPERIAL TRANSPORT VESSEL — MERIDIAN. Leia repeated the name quietly.

For the first time since arriving on Coruscant, they had something more useful than a mysterious code. A ship. A real vessel moving through known space. Somewhere aboard it, or at the end of its journey, might be the people she had been searching for. The meeting ended shortly before midnight.

Venn arranged to continue the traffic analysis with Cloud City's security specialists, while Threepio remained behind to organize the recovered research files. Lando departed to inspect the city's industrial systems. He had discovered that several old Imperial contractors were still drawing money from accounts the city believed had been closed. He seemed rather enthusiastic about confronting them. Han and Leia returned to the Falcon.

For a while, they sat together in the main hold. Neither spoke. The ship was quiet. Chewbacca was repairing something in the engineering compartment, occasionally punctuating his work with irritated growls. Han looked toward Leia.
"I think I'm starting to hate Imperial laboratories."
"Well, I wasn't a big fan of the last one."
"Still, nice to find out I was helping advance science."
Leia laughed despite herself. Then her expression softened.
"For having to watch that recording again."
Han considered her. Then he shrugged.
"They could've made me watch the entire thing with Lando explaining every mistake he made."
She smiled. Han reached for her hand.
"Vader. Jabba. Whoever those scientists were. They tried to take everything from us."
Leia leaned against him. For several minutes, they sat quietly. Then she spoke.
"Do you think those prisoners know Alderaan is gone?"
"Then somebody's going to have to tell them."
"I don't know how to do that."
Han put his arm around her.

She rested her head against his shoulder. Outside the Falcon, Cloud City's lights glimmered beneath the stars. Somewhere in the galaxy, forty-three people from Alderaan remained prisoners of an Empire that no longer officially existed. And somewhere else, a man named Veyr was continuing experiments begun long before Palpatine became Emperor. Leia thought of the strange recording. I remember the garden. Her father's voice.

Or something that sounded exactly like it. She wondered what the original researchers had discovered. And why the experiment had frightened them enough to abandon it. She had a feeling Luke would want to know. Deep within Cloud City's administrative complex, Commander Venn continued examining the transport records. The Meridian's registration had led her to a second vessel. Then a third.

The ships belonged to different companies, but their ownership records all converged on the same organization. A private logistics consortium. One that had existed for decades. Venn opened its corporate registry. The company had changed names repeatedly. It had survived the Clone Wars, the rise of the Empire, and the collapse of Imperial authority. Its current directors were listed as confidential. But the original corporate charter remained accessible.

Venn stared at the screen. The organization's founder had been a financial holding company. DAMASK HOLDINGS. She frowned. The same name that appeared in the Witness Zero experiment. She opened the original registration. The company had been established more than thirty years earlier. Its first director was listed as Hego Damask. The man whose research had apparently preceded the Emperor's experiments.

The man who had died on the eve of Palpatine's election. Venn examined the ownership history. The company had continued operating after his death. Its assets had been transferred to a private trust. And that trust had eventually been absorbed into the Emperor's personal estate. She leaned back. For a moment, she considered the implications. Palpatine's experiments had not begun with the Empire. They had begun before the Republic fell.

Before the Clone Wars. Before anyone outside the Jedi Order knew that the Sith still existed. And someone had preserved the original research for decades. Venn reached for her communicator. Then stopped. A new entry had appeared in the corporate registry. One added only six days earlier. AUTHORIZED EXECUTOR: CUSTODIAN VEYR. She stared at the name. Then another notification appeared. ARCHIVE ACCESS DETECTED. Venn frowned.

She had disconnected the terminal from the external network. The command key had been copied into an isolated system. There should have been no incoming communications. Yet the screen displayed a new message. THANK YOU FOR LOCATING THE MERIDIAN. Venn's blood ran cold. A second line appeared. YOUR ASSISTANCE HAS BEEN NOTED. Then the terminal went dark.
